Period math must align with the requirements: monthly periods end on the same day of the next month, or on the last day when that date does not exist; annual periods end on the same day and month of the following year, with 29 February clamped to 28 February. Each new period starts exactly where the previous one ends.

Period boundaries are computed by adding one calendar month to the previous end date, clamping to the last day of that month when necessary. The original anchor day is not stored; each period simply begins where the prior one ends.

The time of day is preserved across period boundaries. Renewals process one interval at a time until the period end passes the current moment. Free plan periods advance without generating invoices. Canceled subscriptions whose cancellation date has arrived or passed are moved to the free plan as of that date, with no pending cancellation and no invoice. A single plan_changed event is published from paid to free.

If a subscription is canceled before its current period ends, nothing happens until that period expires. When the cancellation date has already passed, the subscription ends immediately without renewing any intervening periods. The plan_changed event to free is emitted whenever the subscription transitions from its current paid plan to free.

Cancellation takes precedence over period expiration. If both a period end and a cancellation date have passed, the subscription moves to the free plan immediately without generating renewal invoices.

The system should check for cancellation first before attempting any renewal. A subscription with status canceled but no cancelAt date is unusual and may be skipped. Trialing and past_due statuses are left untouched.

Invoice numbers must be unique within each workspace. The listInvoices query should order by periodStart descending, then by createdAt descending to handle prorations and renewals in the same period. Each invoice stores the workspace, a unique number, amount in cents, USD currency, period start and end dates, and a null paidAt.

Each invoice is published once as a billing.invoice_issued event. The audit log records this action with the subscription as the subject. A notification of kind invoice_issued is sent to the workspace owner only.

For mid-period changes, proration calculates the full-period amount of the change scaled by days left divided by days in the period, rounded down to whole cents. Days left are counted from the moment of the change to the period end, treating partial days as full; none remain once the period ends.

A charge of zero produces no invoice. Prorated invoices cover the current period and are issued like renewal invoices without changing the period itself.

Adding seats to a paid active subscription is charged for the added seats prorated across the period. Removing seats charges nothing and credits nothing. Seat changes on free or trial subscriptions are ignored.

Changing plans between two paid plans while active is prorated by the price difference per seat multiplied by seat count and months remaining.

Downgrades or unchanged plans charge nothing and leave the period untouched. Choosing a plan during a trial costs nothing and preserves the trial period. Leaving free for paid starts a fresh period at that moment with the chosen interval, invoiced in full. Moving to free also charges nothing. Trials expire automatically via a background job, so preserving trialing status during a plan change is unnecessary. When an active paid subscription moves to free, the plan switches immediately and the period continues unchanged with no invoice. Seat changes are only charged for paid active subscriptions.

Seat changes on past_due or canceled subscriptions are ignored and leave the period unchanged. Switching the billing interval while staying on the same paid plan may not charge anything, since the price difference per seat is zero.

The spec treats switching billing intervals on the same paid plan as an unchanged plan, so it charges nothing and leaves the period untouched. For upgrades between paid plans, the charge is the price difference per seat multiplied by seats and months in the current period.

The spec does not clarify whether "months in the period" refers to the subscription's new interval or the interval of the period being charged. This ambiguity needs resolution.

The month multiplier for prorated plan changes will use the subscription's current interval, since the period being billed remains unchanged. The price difference is calculated between the old and new plan prices.
